correctness.rationale: Every admissible set is blockwise independent given its anchor; optimizing each finite block gives exact formula (1). The rank-k averaging inequality gives the sharp 1/2 equivalence and tail estimate (2). For a fixed maximizing anchor, convergence of norms plus coordinates forces limsup of every far tail to vanish, giving the coordinatewise Kadec implication. Fatou, diagonal compactness and finite equinorming prove the if-and-only-if criterion. Uniform weight on separated full blocks proves the failure of each (λ,γ), λ<1/2 and γ>0. The universal proof is analytic; the checker provides finite independent consistency checks.

value.rationale: The October 2026 work seeks structural criteria for replacing equinorming of A−A by equinorming of A. This example proves the replacement for an entire explicit Banach space that fails every positive near-directedness condition with λ<1/2, showing that the published combinatorial sufficient condition is not necessary. The exact norm formula and optimal 1/2 comparison provide reproducible geometry, and the coordinatewise Kadec estimate isolates the operative mechanism beyond mere ℓ1-equivalence.
